area.title: What are you importing and commodity details
area.scope: Commodity and species selection (the search, the selection panel, the commodity and species lists for live animals and germinal products, removing commodities) and the commodity (consignment) details page: number of animals, packages, gross weight, storage temperature, their validation and completeness. Stops at animal identification and the reason for import. Includes the high-risk plants frontend's commodity type, commodities list and commodity details pages and its commodity rulings, where a row changes the same page plants also has.

sources.role: the owner's decisions: outranks every other source. Search boxes use the real frontend's accessible component with MDM's entries. JavaScript behaviour follows the toolbox rule with graceful degradation; JavaScript-only prototype behaviour, pop-ups included, waits on design in its own theme. Commodity catalogue and search wait on MDM; transporter management waits on requirements; the INS dashboard's summary information waits on its requirements. The overview, review, declaration and confirmation are set-owned, and shared parts change add-only. Where plants has the same page or behaviour, the same increment changes it. Each notification list is reframed in its own frontend. The report groups work as ready or blocked. Claims marked as the orchestrator's apply Sam's principles and are not his rulings; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-templates covers templates and the dashboard narrowing.

claims.statement: Sam rules that the prototype's search and autocomplete controls are not accessible and not production grade, because they are AI-generated prototype code rather than GDS components.

claims.statement: Sam rules that for a search box the precedence is not 'prototype always wins': the component used may be the one already in the real frontends, where it has been deemed accessible.
claims.quote: only use a version of auto complete or search or whatever that has been deemed accessible and meets our requirements. If it has been, the sort of precedence needs to be a little bit different than prototype always wins. In terms of the component being used, it might be the one that's actually in the frontend or frontends.

claims.statement: Sam rules that the prototype's JavaScript behaviour is not GDS compliant and is not to be blindly replicated by adding lots of JavaScript to the frontend, for accessibility and maintainability reasons.
claims.quote: the prototype is doing stuff with JavaScript that is not GDS compliant. This isn't stuff that can just be blindly replicated by chucking a tonne of JavaScript in the frontend. ... 'Do things like add all this JavaScript stuff for accessibility concerns and maintainability concerns.'

claims.statement: Sam rules that GDS components are the toolbox, and where one is not available another tested, accessible government library (such as Ministry of Justice or Scottish Government) is used.
claims.quote: We really try to strictly head here to GDS components as a toolbox, and where that's not available, use other government libraries like a Ministry of Justice or a Scottish Government component that has been tested and meets accessibility requirements.

claims.statement: Sam rules there is a graceful degradation requirement: CSS and JavaScript may enhance behaviour, but every page must work without JavaScript, so the prototype's way of doing things may not be possible or wanted in the real service.
claims.quote: We've got a graceful degradation requirement on this, like any other GDS project, which means you can use things like CSS and JavaScript to enhance behaviour, but you need graceful degradation. It needs to be able to work without JavaScript, and that means that the way things are done in the prototype may not be possible or even desired in the real thing.

claims.statement: Sam rules that, as a pre-step for these increments, three questions are answered: is it possible with off-the-shelf GDS; if not, with other complementary off-the-shelf components; if not, why is the atypical thing strongly required. At that point it goes back to design to push back.
claims.quote: Almost as a pre-step for some of these increments, we need to get answers to that stuff: - Is it possible using off-the-shelf GDS? - If it isn't, is it using available, off-the-shelf, other complementary components? - If it isn't, why is this atypical thing strongly required? At that point, we go back to design and say, 'Come on, we don't need this.'

claims.statement: A behaviour the prototype gives with JavaScript is built only if it passes these tests in order: GOV.UK Frontend's components and patterns first; then another tested government library (Ministry of Justice, HMRC, Scottish Government); otherwise it goes back to design, which must say why it is strongly needed.
claims.quote: GOV.UK Frontend's components and patterns are used first. Where they have nothing, another tested government library is used, such as the Ministry of Justice's, HMRC's or the Scottish Government's. Where neither has anything, the behaviour goes back to design, which must say why it is strongly needed.
claims.note: Marked 'Sam (point 3)'. HMRC is named in claim 5 but not in Sam's quote, which names Ministry of Justice and Scottish Government only; the examples are illustrative ('like').

claims.statement: Nothing other than a DR1 judgement on the same difference or a real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides the prototype.
claims.quote: Only a DR1 judgement or a real constraint the prototype can't express (persistence, validation, auth, cross-service behaviour) overrides it.
claims.note: New. In particular, what a real service does today is not on its own a reason to depart from the prototype.

claims.statement: Questions for people are kept to a minimum.
claims.quote: Decisions: keep questions for people to a minimum.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: A question for people is raised only when a difference is truly exceptional and neither the prototype default nor a DR1 judgement settles it.
claims.quote: Raise one only when a difference is truly exceptional and neither the default nor DR1 settles it.
claims.note: New. Both conditions must hold. 'The default' is read as the prototype-wins default from the Precedence paragraph.

claims.statement: Increments are grouped into themes, and the themes are drawn from the evidence.
claims.quote: Themes: group the increments into themes based on the evidence.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: Each theme's boundary is set by the code it touches.
claims.quote: Draw the boundaries by the code each one touches
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: Themes can be built in parallel on separate machines without pull requests that conflict with each other.
claims.quote: so themes can be built in parallel on separate machines without conflicting PRs.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: The ruling's DR1 paragraph has an elision marked [...]: what the omitted words said about the DR1 parity backlog is not recorded.
The ruling does not say what makes a difference 'truly exceptional', so when a question for people is warranted is left open.

The ruling limits DR1 use to clashes between 'the real frontend' and the prototype; it does not say which frontend that is, or whether DR1 judgements apply to differences in the INS frontend, the backends or other repos.
The ruling does not say which override wins when a DR1 judgement and a real constraint the prototype cannot express point different ways on the same difference.
The ruling does not say what a real service does where a real constraint overrides the prototype: whether it keeps today's behaviour or matches the prototype as closely as the constraint allows.
The ruling does not say whether a feature or behaviour a real service has that Design Release 2.1 does not show at all counts as a difference to remove, or is left alone.
The ruling does not say what to do where the code two themes need to touch overlaps, so no boundary keeps their pull requests from conflicting.

The search query is trimmed of surrounding whitespace, and results are listed only when the trimmed query is at least 3 characters long.
claims.quote:
export const MIN_SEARCH_LENGTH = 3

export const normaliseQuery = (value) => String(value ?? '').trim()

export const isSearchable = (query) =>
  normaliseQuery(query).length >= MIN_SEARCH_LENGTH

claims.statement: On first load the search page lists no commodities or tick boxes: the page lists nothing of its own accord until a long-enough query is entered.

Empty until the query is long enough — the

claims.statement: A query matches a commodity name or species label when its words, case-insensitively and split on any non-alphanumeric character, are a consecutive run of word-prefixes in that text (so 'tau' matches 'Bos taurus' and 'bos tau' matches only in that order).
claims.quote:
A query matches text when its words are a run of word-prefixes in that text.
 * So 'tau' matches 'Bos taurus' on its second word, and 'bos tau' matches only
 * where the two words run in that order.

claims.statement: A query also matches a commodity when the commodity code starts with the query (so '010' narrows to the 0101/0102 range).
claims.quote:
Commodity codes are digit strings, so they match on prefix rather than on
 * whole words — '010' narrows to the 0101/0102 range the way a trader expects.

claims.statement: When the query matches a commodity's name or code, every species under that commodity is listed; otherwise only the species whose own label matches are listed.
claims.quote:
Name or code hits the whole commodity, so every species under it stays in
// the results; otherwise only the species that match on their own.

claims.statement: A species is matched on the label the trader is shown, so its English common name is searchable as well as its scientific name.
claims.quote:
A species matches on the label the trader is shown, so the common name in front of the
// scientific name is searchable rather than decorative.

// line they can still see keeps the rest of its answers.

sources.role: how the real services behave end to end today

claims.statement: The commodity selection page is opened from the notification overview by the task link 'What are you importing?', and lives at /live-animals/notifications/{reference}/commodities.
claims.ref: trace 23432 test action pw:api@50 (click) and pw:api@51; snapshot call@764 frame URL
claims.quote: getByRole('link', { name: 'What are you importing?', exact: true })

claims.statement: Saving the 'Origin of the import' page redirects straight to the commodity selection page.
claims.quote: POST http://localhost:3000/live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-NZPDZ0/origin -> 302 /live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-NZPDZ0/commodities
claims.note: Seen in every trace's setup. The tests then navigate to the overview themselves, so the commodity page rendered on that redirect is not the one exercised.

claims.statement: The commodity selection page's browser title is 'What are you importing? - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
claims.quote: What are you importing? - Import notification service - GOV.UK

claims.statement: The commodity selection page shows the caption 'About the consignment' above the H1 'What are you importing?'.
claims.quote: About the consignment / What are you importing?

claims.statement: The commodity selection page shows an inset text telling the user each health certificate needs its own notification.
claims.quote: A separate notification is required for each health certificate. Consignments that do not require a health certificate must still be notified.

claims.statement: The commodity selection page has one search field, labelled 'Search for a commodity' (medium label), a type=search input named commoditySearch, three-quarters width.
claims.ref: trace 23432 snapshot call@764; trace 66568 class list (INPUT#commoditySearch govuk-input govuk-!-width-three-quarters)
claims.quote: Search for a commodity

claims.statement: The search field's hint says the user can search by commodity name, commodity code or species name, and must enter at least 3 characters.
claims.quote: You can search by commodity name (for example, Cow), commodity code (0102), or species name (Bos taurus). Enter at least 3 characters.

claims.statement: A secondary 'Search' button runs the search by posting the form back to the same page, which re-renders with the results (no client-side lookup).
claims.ref: trace 2d57c test actions pw:api@52-53; trace 0e33b network POST /commodities -> 200; button name=action value=search
claims.quote: POST http://localhost:3000/live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-NZPDZ0/commodities -> 200

claims.statement: Before any search, the commodity selection page lists no species checkboxes and shows no selection panel.
claims.ref: trace 23432 expect@54 (checkbox count 0) and expect@55 (#commodity-selection count 0); snapshot call@764
claims.quote: Expect "toHaveCount" getByRole('checkbox')

claims.statement: A query shorter than three characters ('Bo') lists no species and shows no message at all: neither 'No results found' nor an error.
claims.ref: trace 7c5a8 test actions pw:api@52-53, expect@54; snapshot call@924 (search value 'Bo', no results block)
claims.quote: Enter at least 3 characters.
claims.note: The absence of any message is read from the rendered page after the search; the test asserts only the zero checkbox count.

claims.statement: Search results are grouped by commodity: each group is a fieldset whose small legend reads '<commodity name> (<commodity code>)', holding small checkboxes, one per species, each labelled '<common name> (<scientific name>)'.
claims.ref: trace 2d57c snapshot call@915 and expect@54-58; class list govuk-checkboxes--small, govuk-fieldset__legend--s
claims.quote: Cow (0102) ... Domestic cattle (Bos taurus)

claims.statement: Searching '0102' returns the group 'Cow (0102)' with four species: American bison (Bison bison), Cattle (Bos spp.), Domestic cattle (Bos taurus) and Water buffalo (Bubalus bubalis).
claims.quote: Cow (0102) American bison (Bison bison) Cattle (Bos spp.) Domestic cattle (Bos taurus) Water buffalo (Bubalus bubalis)

claims.statement: Searching '0101' returns the group 'Horse (0101)' with one species, Horse (Equus caballus).
claims.quote: Horse (0101) Horse (Equus caballus)

claims.statement: Searching '01061900' returns two groups that share that code: 'Cat (01061900)' with Cat (Felis catus) and 'Dog (01061900)' with Dog (Canis lupus familiaris).
claims.quote: Cat (01061900) Cat (Felis catus) Dog (01061900) Dog (Canis lupus familiaris)

claims.statement: Searching '0301' returns the group 'Fish (0301)' with one species, Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar).
claims.quote: Fish (0301) Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar)

claims.statement: Search matches on species name, including a partial one: 'Bos taurus' returns only Domestic cattle under 'Cow (0102)', 'Felis catus' returns Cat under 'Cat (01061900)', and 'Salmo' returns Atlantic salmon under 'Fish (0301)'.
claims.ref: trace 66568 snapshots call@850 and call@856; trace 290a2 snapshot call@810
claims.quote: Domestic cattle (Bos taurus)
claims.note: Search by commodity name (for example 'Cow'), which the hint offers, was never exercised: see trace-e2e-p5-038.

claims.statement: Each species checkbox is submitted as field 'species' with a value of the form '<commodity>|<number>', so a choice identifies a commodity and a numbered species within it.
claims.ref: trace 2d57c snapshot call@915 (inputs id species, species-2..4); call@937 (species-group-2 for the second group)
claims.quote: value="Cow|1148346"
claims.note: The values (Cow|716661, Cow|1388624, Cow|1148346, Cow|749313, Horse|822332, Cat|923501, Dog|923502, Fish|801204) are verbatim; that the number is a reference-data species identifier is inferred.

claims.statement: When a query matches nothing ('zzz'), the page says 'No results found' and lists no checkboxes.
claims.quote: No results found

claims.statement: Once species are chosen, the page shows a selection panel headed with a running count ('1 selected', '2 selected') listing each choice as '<commodity> (<code>): <common name> (<scientific name>)', with the commodity part in bold.
claims.ref: trace 66568 snapshot call@868 (#commodity-selection); trace 290a2 expect@57-58, snapshot call@810
claims.quote: 2 selected Cow (0102): Domestic cattle (Bos taurus) Cat (01061900): Cat (Felis catus)

claims.statement: The selection panel is written by the server, so ticking a box does not update it at once; it appears on the next page render, such as the next search.
claims.ref: commodities.spec.ts test 'counts what has been chosen and clears it on request'; trace 290a2 pw:api@54-56 then expect@57
claims.quote: The panel is written on the server, so it appears on the next render.
claims.note: The quote is the spec's own comment; the trace bears it out (the panel first appears in snapshot call@810, after the Salmo search).

claims.statement: A choice made under one query is kept when the user searches again: after ticking Bos taurus and searching 'Felis catus', the panel shows '1 selected' with Domestic cattle while the results show only Cat.
claims.ref: trace 66568 test actions pw:api@52-57; snapshot call@856
claims.quote: 1 selected Cow (0102): Domestic cattle (Bos taurus)

claims.statement: Choices not on screen under the current query are carried in the form as hidden 'selection' fields, one per choice.
claims.ref: trace 66568 snapshots call@856, call@868, call@878, call@884
claims.quote: INPUT hidden name=selection value=Cow|1148346
claims.note: Inferred from the DOM: a choice whose checkbox is on screen is not repeated as a hidden field (call@878 carries only Cat while Cow's checkbox is shown ticked).

claims.statement: A secondary 'Clear all' button in the selection panel removes every choice; the panel then disappears.
claims.ref: trace 290a2 pw:api@59, expect@60; snapshot call@816 (no panel); button name=action value=clear
claims.quote: Clear all

claims.statement: Saving several species chosen under different queries persists all of them: Bos taurus and Felis catus both become commodity lines.
claims.ref: trace 66568 pw:api@58, expect@59; snapshot call@860 (two table rows, two sections)
claims.quote: accepts and persists multiple commodity-species pairs found under different queries

claims.statement: Coming back to the commodity selection page after saving shows the saved choices in the selection panel with an empty search box and no results.
claims.quote: 2 selected

claims.statement: A saved species shows ticked when a later search brings it back on screen.
claims.ref: trace 66568 expect@68 and expect@71; snapshots call@878 and call@884 (checkbox CHECKED)
claims.quote: Expect "toBeChecked" getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Bos taurus' })

claims.statement: Pressing 'Save and continue' with nothing chosen re-shows the page with an error summary titled 'There is a problem' whose one entry, 'Select a commodity', links to the search field.
claims.ref: trace 725f7 pw:api@52, expect@53-54; snapshot call@904 (error summary link href #commoditySearch)
claims.quote: There is a problem Select a commodity

claims.statement: With nothing chosen, the error is also shown inline on the search field as 'Error: Select a commodity', and the field's form group takes the error style.
claims.quote: Error: Select a commodity

claims.statement: When the commodity selection page shows an error, its browser title is prefixed 'Error: '.
claims.ref: trace 725f7 snapshot of /commodities after submit, TITLE element
claims.quote: Error: What are you importing? - Import notification service - GOV.UK

claims.statement: 'Save and continue' with at least one species chosen saves and redirects to the commodity details page (/consignment-details).
claims.ref: trace 0e33b network POST /commodities -> 302; test action pw:api@56 waits for 'Commodity details'
claims.quote: POST http://localhost:3000/live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-NZPDZ0/commodities -> 302 /live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-NZPDZ0/consignment-details

claims.statement: The commodity selection page has a 'Help with commodity codes' details component explaining commodity codes in three paragraphs.
claims.quote: Help with commodity codes / Commodity codes are internationally recognised reference numbers. A commodity code describes a specific product when importing or exporting goods. You can look up commodity codes using the Trade Tariff tool (opens in a new tab).

claims.statement: The help text links to the Trade Tariff tool at https://www.gov.uk/trade-tariff, opening in a new tab.
claims.ref: trace 0e33b snapshot call@856, a.govuk-link href=https://www.gov.uk/trade-tariff target=_blank
claims.quote: Trade Tariff tool (opens in a new tab)

claims.statement: The commodity selection, commodity details and additional details pages each end with a primary 'Save and continue' button, a secondary 'Save and return to overview' button, and a 'Cancel and return to overview' link to the notification overview.
claims.ref: trace 66568 snapshots call@836 and call@860; trace 6c9ed snapshot call@730; Save and return button name=exit value=hub
claims.quote: Save and continue / Save and return to overview / Cancel and return to overview

claims.statement: The back link on all three pages goes to the notification overview (/live-animals/notifications/{reference}), not to the previous page.
claims.ref: trace 66568 snapshots call@836 and call@860 (a.govuk-back-link href); trace 6c9ed snapshot call@730
claims.quote: Back

claims.statement: The commodity details page is a hub task of its own: its back link returns to the overview, and the selection is reopened from the overview task 'What are you importing?'.
claims.ref: commodities.spec.ts comment in 'accepts and persists multiple commodity-species pairs'; trace 66568 pw:api@60-62, expect@61
claims.quote: Commodity details is a hub task of its own, so its back link returns to the overview.

claims.statement: Above the form, all three pages show a journey strip with a blue 'Draft' tag and the notification reference in bold (for example GBN-AG-26-DC83HM).
claims.quote: Draft GBN-AG-26-DC83HM

claims.statement: The three pages use only govuk-frontend components (inset text, input, button, details, checkboxes, fieldset, table, radios, error summary) apart from two custom classes: 'app-journey-strip', a wrapper around a standard tag and bold text, and 'app-link-button', a submit button styled as a link for 'Remove'.
claims.quote: DIV app-journey-strip govuk-!-margin-bottom-4 / BUTTON govuk-link app-link-button
claims.note: A link-styled form button has no standard govuk-frontend component; the strip could be a plain govuk-tag plus govuk-body text.

claims.statement: No trace searches by commodity name (for example 'Cow'), though the hint offers it, so the result shape for a name search is not shown.
No trace presses 'Search' with an empty query or shows any search validation message; what an empty or too-short search tells the user (beyond the hint) is not shown.

The browser never calls a reference-data or commodity API itself; the commodity search is answered by the frontend server, so the back-end lookup it makes (and its source) is not visible in the traces.
claims.ref: network logs of traces 0e33b, 66568, 6c9ed, 1c358 (only same-origin page requests)

claims.statement: Every form on these pages posts to its own URL with browser validation switched off (novalidate), so validation is done on the server.
claims.ref: trace 6c9ed snapshots, FORM method=post novalidate on /commodities, /consignment-details, /additional-details
claims.quote: FORM {"method":"post","novalidate":""}

claims.statement: Each form carries a hidden concurrencyToken that rises as the notification is saved (1 on first selection, 2 after the commodity save, 4 on additional details, up to 8 in the scope trace), which suggests saves are guarded against concurrent edits.
claims.ref: trace 1c358 snapshots call@78 (2), call@96 (4), call@114 (5), call@134 (8); trace 66568 call@836 (1)
claims.quote: INPUT hidden name=concurrencyToken value=2
claims.note: No trace shows a concurrency conflict, so what the user sees on one is a gap.

claims.statement: The commodity details page's browser title is 'Commodity details - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
claims.quote: Commodity details - Import notification service - GOV.UK

claims.statement: The page at /consignment-details shows the caption 'About the consignment' and the H1 'Commodity details' (not 'consignment details').
claims.quote: About the consignment / Commodity details

claims.statement: The commodity details page opens with a table captioned 'Selected commodities' with columns 'Commodity code', 'Common name' and 'Actions', one row per commodity line (for example '0102 | Cow | Remove').
claims.ref: trace ca7de snapshot call@840; trace 66568 snapshot call@860
claims.quote: Selected commodities Commodity code Common name Actions 0102 Cow Remove Cow

claims.statement: Each table row has a 'Remove' action, a submit button styled as a link whose hidden text names the commodity ('Remove Cow'), in a form of its own above the details form.
claims.ref: trace 66568 snapshot call@860: BUTTON govuk-link app-link-button name=action value=remove:0 and value=remove-species:1
claims.quote: Remove Cow
claims.note: The two rows carry different action values, 'remove:0' for Cow and 'remove-species:1' for Cat, so the two rows may remove different things (a whole line or one species). No trace presses Remove: see trace-e2e-p5-058.

claims.statement: Under the table, an 'Add another commodity' link returns to the commodity selection page.
claims.quote: Add another commodity

claims.quote: Cow (0102) Bos taurus ... Cat (01061900) Felis catus

claims.quote: Number of animals

claims.quote: Number of packages (when required) / Such as crates, bags or boxes

claims.quote: Number of animals

claims.statement: Entering 1 animal and 5 packages and pressing 'Save and continue' saves without error and returns to the notification overview.
claims.quote: POST http://localhost:3000/live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-NZPDZ0/consignment-details -> 302 /live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-NZPDZ0

claims.statement: Selecting a further species adds a new commodity line rather than replacing the earlier ones: after Felis catus was saved, adding Bos taurus gives two lines.
claims.quote: Each call ADDS a commodity line.

claims.statement: The selection panel on a return visit lists earlier lines' species ('1 selected', Cat) while a new search offers the next species unticked, which shows selection works per species and adds to the saved lines.
claims.quote: 1 selected Cat (01061900): Cat (Felis catus)

claims.statement: According to the tests, the number of animals blocks saving on every commodity line, so each line's count must be filled before the page hands back to the overview.

claims.quote: The animal count is save-blocking on every line, so each box the consignment page is showing — the lines added on earlier passes included — is filled before it hands back to the hub.

claims.statement: No trace presses 'Remove' on the commodity details page, so what removal does (a whole line or one species), whether it asks for confirmation, and where it lands are not shown.

claims.statement: No trace presses 'Save and return to overview' on any of the three pages, so whether it saves partial answers, or validates them, is not shown.
